title: Factual position on Ken–Betwa Link Project
body_text:
There are certain media reports which have claimed that symbolic protests such as “Chita Andolan”, “Fansi Pradarshan” and “Jal Satyagraha” are being organized in certain areas of Madhya Pradesh against the Ken–Betwa Link Project, alleging displacement of tribal families without compensation.
The allegations that affected families have not been compensated or rehabilitated are incorrect and misleading. Most eligible families have received full compensation and rehabilitation benefits, and only procedural formalities remain in a few cases. The Government of India, Government of Madhya Pradesh, and the Ken–Betwa Link Project Authority remain fully committed to ensuring transparent, just, and time-bound compensation and dignified rehabilitation for all genuinely affected families.
The fact of the matter is that the Ken–Betwa Link Project, India’s first major river-linking initiative under the National Perspective Plan, aims to transfer surplus water from the Ken River to the Betwa River to provide irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydropower benefits to the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
The project will ensure irrigation for 10.62 lakh hectares, drinking water for nearly 62 lakh people, and 103 MW of hydropower generation. Of the total estimated cost of ₹44,604.99 crore, ₹12,445.85 crore has been spent up to July 2026. The project is being implemented by the Ken–Betwa Link Project Authority.
Land acquisition, rehabilitation, and resettlement activities are being carried out strictly in accordance with the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, and the Special Rehabilitation Package approved by the Government of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September 2023. Compensation for acquired land is being provided either as per the Act or at ₹12.50 lakh per hectare, whichever is higher. Compensation for houses, trees, wells, tube wells, and other immovable assets has been determined as per statutory provisions.
Eligible families are being provided ₹7 lakh for rural plots and ₹6.50 lakh for urban plots, while those opting out of plots receive ₹12.50 lakh as one-time assistance. Additional financial support is being extended to eligible Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe families in Scheduled Areas to ensure a fair and balanced rehabilitation process.
It is also stated that as of July 2026, awards amounting to ₹360.66 crore have been passed for 10,913 affected persons (agricultural land compensation), of which ₹320.45 crore (88.85%) has already been disbursed. For habitation areas (house related properties), ₹149.63 crore has been awarded, with 93.97% disbursed. A total of 5,039 affected families to be rehabilitated have been identified, with awards of ₹629.87 crore, out of which ₹590.74 crore (93.78%) has been paid. Remaining payments will be made upon completion of legal formalities. Continuous verification of land records is being undertaken to ensure that no eligible family is deprived of benefits.
Under the Jan Vishwas programme, the district administration recently organized a special camp at Karaondia to address issues of displaced families. Approvals were granted for applications related to animal husbandry, social security, poverty line, Ladli Behna and Ladli Lakshmi schemes. Health services were provided to 178 persons, AYUSH medicines were distributed, handpumps were repaired, and scholarship mapping and book distribution were conducted for students. In the last ten days alone, ₹10.42 crore has been sanctioned to 86 affected persons.
These facts clearly demonstrate that the protests highlighted in the media are misleading, and names of individuals participating in recent protests do not appear in the list of project-affected families, land records, or compensation registers. These activities are largely being conducted by external elements with the intent to circulate misleading and factually incorrect narratives regarding the project.
***
ND

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti has rebutted media reports of tribal protests ("Chita Andolan", "Jal Satyagraha") against the Ken–Betwa Link Project in Madhya Pradesh, asserting that allegations of non-payment of compensation are misleading. It states that most eligible families have received compensation under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 and a Special Rehabilitation Package approved in September 2023, with over 88-94% of awarded amounts already disbursed as of July 2026. The project, India's first major river-interlinking initiative, aims to irrigate 10.62 lakh hectares, supply drinking water to 62 lakh people, and generate 103 MW hydropower, at an estimated cost of ₹44,604.99 crore.
enrichment.context:
The Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP) is the pilot project under India's National Perspective Plan (NPP) for interlinking of rivers, first conceived in 1980 to transfer water from surplus basins to deficit ones. It seeks to divert water from the Ken River to the Betwa River to address chronic drought in the Bundelkhand region spanning Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. The project involves construction of the Daudhan Dam within the Panna Tiger Reserve, which has made it environmentally and socially contentious, involving forest diversion, wildlife habitat loss, and displacement of tribal and rural communities—issues that have historically delayed river-linking projects in India.

The rehabilitation framework invoked here—the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act (RFCTLARR), 2013—is the standard national law governing land acquisition compensation, but state governments can supplement it with special packages, as Madhya Pradesh did in 2023. Given past controversies over interlinking projects (environmental clearances, displacement, and inter-state water sharing), this project is often cited as a test case for whether India's ambitious river-linking programme can be implemented without major social and ecological costs. The PIB clarification indicates the ongoing friction between official rehabilitation data and grassroots protest narratives, a recurring feature of large infrastructure projects in India.

prelims_questions.question: The Ken–Betwa Link Project, mentioned frequently in news, is being implemented under which of the following?
options: National Perspective Plan for interlinking of rivers
prelims_questions.explanation: The Ken–Betwa Link Project is India's first major river-linking initiative under the National Perspective Plan (NPP), aiming to transfer surplus water from the Ken to the Betwa river.

prelims_questions.question: Under which legislation is land acquisition and compensation being carried out for the Ken–Betwa Link Project, as per the PIB release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that land acquisition, rehabilitation, and resettlement are being carried out as per the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 and the Special Rehabilitation Package approved by Madhya Pradesh in 2023.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives and significance of the Ken–Betwa Link Project as a pilot for India's river interlinking programme. What social and environmental challenges does it illustrate?

Examine the adequacy of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 in ensuring fair compensation and rehabilitation for communities displaced by large infrastructure projects in India, with reference to the Ken–Betwa Link Project.

study_notes.reason: The release carries hard, testable facts about India's first river-interlinking project (NPP origins, Daudhan Dam siting inside Panna Tiger Reserve, RFCTLARR-based compensation formula, project targets) while also offering genuine analytical material on the recurring tension between official rehabilitation claims and grassroots displacement narratives, and on the development-versus-conservation trade-off inherent in river-linking schemes.

prelims.point: Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP) is India's first major river-interlinking project, implemented as the pilot under the National Perspective Plan (NPP) for interlinking of rivers, originally conceived in 1980.
prelims.why_important: UPSC frequently tests 'first/pilot' facts about major infrastructure schemes and their originating policy framework (NPP, 1980).

prelims.point: The project's Daudhan Dam, which enables the Ken-to-Betwa water transfer, is being constructed within the Panna Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh.
prelims.why_important: Location of a major dam inside a Tiger Reserve is a classic fact UPSC uses to link infrastructure projects with protected-area and wildlife-conservation issues.

prelims.point: Land acquisition and rehabilitation for KBLP are governed by the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, supplemented by Madhya Pradesh's Special Rehabilitation Package approved on 13 September 2023.
prelims.why_important: RFCTLARR, 2013 is the standard national land acquisition/compensation law and its interplay with state-specific packages is a common prelims distinction.

prelims.point: KBLP is designed to provide irrigation to 10.62 lakh hectares, drinking water to about 62 lakh people, and generate 103 MW of hydropower, at an estimated cost of ₹44,604.99 crore, implemented by the Ken–Betwa Link Project Authority.
prelims.why_important: Scheme statistics (beneficiaries, capacity, cost, implementing agency) are typical objective-question material for flagship infrastructure projects.

mains.point: The gap between the government's compensation/disbursement data and continuing grassroots protests (Chita Andolan, Jal Satyagraha) illustrates a recurring governance challenge: official rehabilitation statistics versus lived experience of project-affected communities.
mains.theme: Transparency and trust deficit in large infrastructure projects
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on why large infrastructure projects face resistance despite official compliance claims, and on mechanisms to build trust between state agencies and displaced communities.

mains.point: River-interlinking projects like KBLP embody a structural trade-off between water security/irrigation benefits and ecological costs such as forest diversion and loss of tiger habitat.
mains.analytical_use: Applicable to 'discuss the environmental and social costs of river-linking projects in India' type questions, weighing water security against biodiversity loss.

both.concept: RFCTLARR Act, 2013 combined with state Special Rehabilitation Packages as the compensation mechanism for KBLP-affected families.
both.prelims_angle: Testable as the governing central law for land acquisition, with the 2023 MP package as a state-level supplement, including specific compensation figures (₹12.50 lakh/hectare, ₹7 lakh rural plot, etc.).
both.mains_angle: Raises the analytical question of whether statutory compensation frameworks are adequate for genuinely rehabilitating tribal and rural families, and whether disbursement percentages (88-94%) reflect real resettlement or only monetary settlement.

both.concept: Ken–Betwa Link Project as the test case for India's broader National Perspective Plan on river interlinking.
both.prelims_angle: Factual core: NPP's 1980 origin, KBLP's status as first pilot, and its Bundelkhand (MP-UP) target region.
both.mains_angle: Analytically significant as it will determine the feasibility, inter-state cooperation, and environmental viability of extending river-linking to other basins across India.

low_priority.point: Details of the Jan Vishwas special camp at Karaondia (health camps, AYUSH medicine distribution, handpump repairs, scholarship mapping).
low_priority.reason: Routine administrative welfare activity with no distinct examinable content beyond illustrating general rehabilitation outreach.

low_priority.point: Claim that protesters' names do not appear in project-affected family records.
low_priority.reason: A political rebuttal specific to this PIB clarification, not a generalisable or testable fact.

low_priority.point: Granular disbursement percentages for each compensation category (e.g., 93.97% for habitation properties).
low_priority.reason: Overly specific administrative data unlikely to be tested; the broader point of high disbursement is already captured.
